mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES stays near a 10% deficit while TRANSIT remains deeply negative, weekday shopping demand will keep weakening through the next four weeks because fewer commuters pass retail corridors. RETAIL_REC should therefore drift lower or stay flat relative to the last four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite no recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT from the current depressed levels.

mechanism_narrative: A further drop in RESIDENTIAL above the current +13% level implies more time spent at home, which suppresses discretionary trips and reduces retail visits within one to two weeks. The effect should appear first as weaker RETAIL_REC before spreading across the month.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains at or above +13% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is elevated around +14% in the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases within 14 days even though RESIDENTIAL stays elevated for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS falls faster than WORKPLACES, discretionary out-of-home time is shifting away from leisure corridors and toward home-centered activity. That substitution should reduce retail-and-recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall relative to the last four weeks even as PARKS continues to underperform WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT slips below -27% week on week, the city is likely entering a tighter mobility regime that curbs cross-purpose shopping trips. Under that threshold crossing, RETAIL_REC should decline within the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is already near -27.6% in the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or remains unchanged over the next 28 days after TRANSIT drops below -27%.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in GROCERY_PHARM relative to RETAIL_REC indicates demand is being redirected toward essential shopping rather than discretionary retail. If that gap widens further, retail-and-recreation mobility should weaken over the next one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM exceeds RETAIL_REC by at least 15 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 14 days after GROCERY_PHARM moves 15 points above RETAIL_REC.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward move in PARKS during late-winter reopening weeks is a marker of improving outdoor circulation that later spills into retail trips. If PARKS rebounds from its current weakness, RETAIL_REC should improve over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises at least 5 points from its current week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS has been negative and recently improved from -20.9 to -19.1
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its last-four-week mean after PARKS rebounds by at least 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: A synchronized improvement in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT will rebuild daily foot traffic around shopping districts and increase discretionary stopping behavior. This interaction should lift RETAIL_REC within one week and continue over the next month.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise week on week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 7 days after both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise together.

mechanism_narrative: If all three nonessential movement series stay compressed while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated, households are substituting away from discretionary trips and retail demand will keep softening. Under that regime, RETAIL_REC should be lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite persistent low TRANSIT and WORKPLACES with elevated RESIDENTIAL.
